title: R-KV: Redundancy-aware KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Models
one_line_claim: Identifies and removes redundant tokens from KV cache during decoding in reasoning models by jointly balancing importance (via attention weights) and semantic similarity.
method_summary: R-KV compresses KV cache at decoding time by scoring tokens on two axes: importance via attention weights, and redundancy via cosine similarity of key vectors. Jointly selects top-k tokens using Z = lambda*I - (1-lambda)*R to balance both metrics.

key_findings.finding: Reasoning models generate 8-14x longer outputs than ground truth, with 5-7x higher 1-2-gram repetition frequency.
key_findings.quote: Reasoning models generate substantially longer responses with 8-14x more tokens, and show higher word repetition with 5-7x higher frequency.

key_findings.finding: R-KV achieves 105% of full KV cache performance on AIME-24 with only 16% of the KV cache.
key_findings.quote: R-KV even achieves 105% accuracy of the full KV baseline with around 16% of the KV cache.

key_findings.finding: With 34% KV cache budget, R-KV achieves lossless compression on MATH-500, outperforming SnapKV at 60% performance.
key_findings.quote: by selectively retaining only 10-34% of the original KV cache, R-KV achieves comparable performance parity with the uncompressed reasoning model, outperforming state-of-the-art compression baselines, which reaches only 60% of the performance.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both target KV-cache compression during decoding and aim to enable efficient long-sequence inference.
differs_on: R-KV uses attention-based importance and key-vector cosine similarity; HERALD uses per-token logit features (entropy, repetition) for failure prediction.
R-KV proactively removes redundant tokens during decoding; HERALD predicts catastrophic failure onset using XGBoost.
R-KV targets reasoning-specific redundancy in chain-of-thought; HERALD addresses general compression-induced degradation.
